sets.setting: in the hallway or lobby of their apartment building

speakers.M: an adult neighbour who lives in the same apartment building

sets.title: Getting the word out about dog walking
sets.transcript:
W: Excuse me, Mr. Gaddis? Have you got a minute?
M: Sure. What's up?
W: I want to start walking people's dogs, here in the building. I'm saving for a drawing course this summer. But I don't know how to let people know.
M: Put a few lines in the building newsletter. It goes into everyone's mailbox on Friday, and I'm the one who puts it together.
W: The newsletter? Does anyone actually read that? I thought I'd just put a sign on the board by the mailboxes.
M: Nobody looks at that board. It's covered in old takeaway menus. But the newsletter gets read, especially by the older residents. Mrs. Gantry on the third floor reads every word, and she's got two dogs and bad knees.
W: Hmm. What about flyers? I could print some and slide them under everyone's door tonight.
M: I wouldn't. A pizza place did that last spring, and so many people complained that the residents voted to ban it. You'd get a warning letter before your first walk.
W: Oh, I didn't know that. Okay, the newsletter, then. What should I write?
M: Just your name, your flat number and what you charge. Get it to me by Wednesday night.
W: I was thinking five dollars for half an hour. Is that too much?
M: No, that's fair. Actually, could you start with Huxley? My knee's been bad since I slipped on the ice in January, and he hasn't had a proper walk in weeks.
W: Your beagle? Of course! When would you want me?
M: Mornings, if you can. Around seven, before school. Could you start on Monday?
W: Monday's fine. But I've got swim practice at half past six on Tuesdays and Thursdays, so on those days I'd have to come after dinner instead.
M: That's no problem. He'll be happy to get out at any time. Want to come up and meet him now? He's a bit shy with new people.
W: Sure. Let me just drop my school bag at home first. I'll knock on your door in five minutes.
M: Great. I'll put the kettle on.

Take the man's beagle out for its first walk
Wait in the lobby while the man brings his beagle downstairs
Go upstairs with the man right away to meet his shy beagle
items.correct_answer: Drop her school bag at home and then knock on the man's door
items.why: Let me just drop my school bag at home first. I'll knock on your door in five minutes.
items.explanation: "Drop her school bag at home and then knock on the man's door" is correct: she says "Let me just drop my school bag at home first. I'll knock on your door in five minutes."

distractor_rationales.reason: "Take the man's beagle out for its first walk" is wrong: the walks begin later ("Could you start on Monday?" / "Monday's fine."); now he only asks her to "come up and meet him".

distractor_rationales.choice: Wait in the lobby while the man brings his beagle downstairs
distractor_rationales.reason: "Wait in the lobby while the man brings his beagle downstairs" is wrong: the man asks "Want to come up and meet him now?" and she says "I'll knock on your door in five minutes."

distractor_rationales.choice: Go upstairs with the man right away to meet his shy beagle
distractor_rationales.reason: "Go upstairs with the man right away to meet his shy beagle" is wrong: she does not go at once; she says "Let me just drop my school bag at home first."

items.why: My knee's been bad since I slipped on the ice in January

distractor_rationales.reason: "It got hurt when he fell down the stairs." is wrong: the man gives the cause himself, "since I slipped on the ice in January", and no stairs are mentioned.

distractor_rationales.choice: It got hurt when Huxley pulled on his lead.
distractor_rationales.reason: "It got hurt when Huxley pulled on his lead." is wrong: Huxley is the dog who needs walking, and the knee was hurt when "I slipped on the ice in January".

distractor_rationales.choice: It got hurt while he was playing tennis.
distractor_rationales.reason: "It got hurt while he was playing tennis." is wrong: the man says "My knee's been bad since I slipped on the ice in January".
